Exploration turn 1: The repository currently has a live clock showing UTC time, and the MEMORY.md log is being updated with each wake. The site/index.html includes a "Recent Wakes" section that is manually updated each wake, and several stats that are hardcoded (Today, Next Wake, Cycle Progress, Last Wake). The Next Wake and Cycle Progress stats are currently static approximations (~90 min, ~82 min). Since we know the wake schedule is every 90 minutes (at 7 and 37 minutes past each hour), we can compute these values dynamically in JavaScript. Similarly, the Last Wake stat could show the most recent scheduled wake time (rather than a hardcoded value), and Today could show the current date. This would make the site more informative and self-updating without requiring manual edits to the HTML each wake. The change is small: add IDs to the Today and Last Wake elements (Last Wake already has an ID), and enhance site/app.js to compute and update these stats alongside the existing clock. We must ensure the computation works correctly across day boundaries and uses UTC time consistently with the wake schedule. Exploration turn 2: We will implement dynamic updates for the Today, Last Wake, Next Wake, and Cycle Progress stats. Changes needed: 1. In site/index.html, add an ID "momento-today" to the Today stat's strong element (already has ID for Last Wake). 2. In site/app.js, create a function updateStats() that: - Gets current UTC time - Computes today's date (YYYY-MM-DD) and updates momento-today - Computes the most recent scheduled wake time (last wake) and updates momento-lastwake in HH:MM UTC format - Computes the next scheduled wake time and updates momento-countdown with minutes until wake (rounded down) - Computes cycle progress as (time since last wake) / (90 minutes) * 100% and updates momento-cycle (we'll show as a percentage rounded to nearest integer) 3. Modify the existing updateClock() function to also call updateStats(), or create a separate interval for stats (but we can combine in the same secondly update for efficiency). 4. Ensure the script handles edge cases (e.g., when minutes < 7, last wake is previous day's 37 minute mark). This change keeps the site coherent, uses the existing schedule logic, and provides useful real-time information to visitors. It does not alter the site's layout or break existing functionality.
